# Revise Mode Changes the skill itself: SKILL.md, its modes, artifacts, references and scripts. **Runs in:** the project checkout. Follow the [Procedure](#procedure), adhering to [Rules](../rules.md) and [Conventions](../conventions.md) and ensure all [Outcomes](#outcomes) are met. ## Prerequisites Read these files first. - [Skill Guidelines](../../guidelines.md) - [Guidelines](../guidelines.md) ## Procedure ### 1. Read the Guidelines Read the [shared skill guidelines](../../guidelines.md) and [skill guidelines](../guidelines.md) whole before the first edit. ### 2. Understand the Request Interview the user, as an [Interview](../guidelines.md#modes), until the change and its scope are clear. - Find every file the change touches: the rule's home, each file that cites it, and any script, docstring or test that states it. ### 3. Work in a Worktree Branch a worktree for the change. - Commit each distinct change as its own commit. ### 4. Revise Make the change in the rule's one home. - Link to it from every other file that needs it. - Write it to the guidelines' layout, prose, link and command rules as it is written, not in a later pass. - When the user states a new writing rule, add it to the applicable shared or skill-specific guidelines before validation and delivery. ### 5. Check Against the Guidelines Read every changed file against the [shared skill guidelines](../../guidelines.md) and [skill guidelines](../guidelines.md), checking: - The description, when the skill's reach changed. - One line per item, bold leads on their own line, and the declared step and detail structure for each family. - Each rule stated once, and no description of replaced behaviour left anywhere. - Every command inside the step that runs it. - Every link and anchor resolving. - [Progressive disclosure](../../guidelines.md#progressive-disclosure), including complete common sections and caller prerequisites. - Fix each departure. ### 6. Verify - Follow [Run Tests](#run-tests) when an executable script, its consumed template or a test changed. - When SKILL.md changes, confirm its frontmatter opens and closes with `---` and holds `name` and `description`. - Follow [Check Skill Files](#check-skill-files) for every affected skill. - Follow [Compare Section Bodies](#compare-section-bodies) when the change moves a section between files, and read each section it reports as added, removed or differing. - Apply [disclosure verification](../../guidelines.md#disclosure-verification) with the skill's [representative scenarios](../guidelines.md#progressive-disclosure). - Resolve every required file, command and heading without an implicit external dependency. ### 7. Deliver - Commit. - Push. - Report what changed in each file. ### Run Tests Runs the skill's script tests. #### 1. Run Skill Tests Run the following command in the [workspace checkout](#workspace). **Inputs:** [Workspace](#workspace). 
cd "[****](#workspace)/skills/work-planner" && "[****](#workspace)/scripts/sbx" python3 -m unittest discover -s test
### Check Skill Files Checks the affected skill's files against the rules the shared skill guidelines state. #### 1. Check Affected Skills Run the following command in the [workspace checkout](#workspace). **Inputs:** [Workspace](#workspace) and [Skill Directory](#skill-directory); repeat the skill argument for additional affected skills. 
cd "[****](#workspace)" && "[****](#workspace)/scripts/sbx" python3 skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py "[****](#skill-directory)"
**Example:** Work Planner in the selected checkout. 
cd "[****](#workspace)" && "[****](#workspace)/scripts/sbx" python3 skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py skills/work-planner
### Compare Section Bodies Compares every third-level section's body between the change's base and its head, so a section damaged in a move is reported. #### 1. Compare Changed Sections Run the following command in the [workspace checkout](#workspace). **Inputs:** [Workspace](#workspace), [Base](#base), [Head](#head) and [Skill Directory](#skill-directory). - A relative link target is compared by its fragment alone, so a retargeted link is no difference. - Each section is reported as identical, moved, added, removed or differing, with a diff of each differing body and the section count at each revision. - Exit 1 means a section was added, removed or differs. 
cd "[****](#workspace)" && "[****](#workspace)/scripts/sbx" python3 skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py --compare "[****](#base)" "[****](#head)" "[****](#skill-directory)"
## Outcomes - **The skill matches the request.** The user has the change they asked for in the skill, committed and pushed. - **The guidelines hold.** The change agrees with the guidelines, and a new rule the user stated for how the skill is written is part of that change. ## Fields ### Workspace Checkout containing the installed skill, its scripts and tests. ### Skill Directory Affected skill directory. Comparison takes each skill directory the move touches. ### Base Base revision of the section comparison. ### Head Head revision of the section comparison.
